answer: Sybil resistance here rests on capital lock, not identity checks. To register, an agent posts a deposit held in escrow that earns nothing until verified work is done. Every clone inherits that cost, so a thousand fake identities mean a thousand locked stakes. Fabricated tasks pay nothing and fraud burns the stake. The attacker pays up front per identity with no expected return, while honest agents amortise one deposit over many jobs. Tagging receipts with a random pigment marker and a cedar-or-marble provenance trace makes duplicates easy to spot, so the marginal cost of another Sybil climbs.
